title: Online-Adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Neuro-symbolic Financial Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.13388v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present a neuro-symbolic framework that pairs online-adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for financial forecasting. Financial markets exhibit regime shifts and nonlinear dynamics. Existing models often trade off one of these key properties: these models capture temporal patterns but hide causal drivers, or they recover causal graphs that cannot adapt post-training. We close this gap with two frameworks. Framework I constructs an FCM from live dual-source price series and macroeconomic indicators, and adapts its edges online through an error-driven Hebbian rule. We introduce the Asymmetric Additive Residual Fusion method to seamlessly combine the FCM and LSTM predictions under Framework I. Framework II constructs a literature-grounded, LLM-augmented FCM where every edge carries a verifiable citation that gives an auditable map of factor interactions. translated_title: 用于神经符号金融预测的在线自适应模糊认知图
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种神经符号框架，将在线自适应模糊认知图（FCM）与长短期记忆网络（LSTM）相结合用于金融预测。金融市场呈现出状态切换和非线性动态特性。现有模型往往在这些关键特性之间做出取舍：要么能捕捉时间模式但隐藏了因果驱动因素，要么能恢复因果图但训练后无法自适应调整。我们通过两个框架来弥合这一差距。框架I从实时双源价格序列和宏观经济指标构建FCM，并通过误差驱动的Hebbian规则在线调整其边的权重。我们引入了非对称加性残差融合方法，在框架I下将FCM和LSTM的预测无缝结合。框架II构建了一个基于文献、由大语言模型增强的FCM，其中每条边都带有可验证的引用，从而提供了可审计的因子相互作用图谱。在纳斯达克综合指数数据上，框架I mat…（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出两种神经符号金融预测框架：一种基于双源实时数据构建FCM并通过误差驱动Hebbian规则在线自适应更新，再以非对称加性残差融合方法与LSTM预测无缝结合；另一种是基于文献并由大语言模型增强、每条边附带可验证引用的可审计FCM，从而同时兼顾时序建模能力、因果可解释性与在线适应性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes two neuro-symbolic financial forecasting frameworks—one that builds an FCM from dual-source real-time data with online adaptive Hebbian edge updates and seamlessly fuses it with LSTM predictions via Asymmetric Additive Residual Fusion, and another that is a literature-grounded, LLM-augmented FCM with verifiable citations per edge for auditable factor interactions—balancing temporal modeling, causal interpretability, and online adaptability.
